prerequisites: Knowledge and abilities in all topics of Radio-link technologies

learning_outcomes.text: Students must know the properties of electromagnetic fields and the main devices that use them and be able to correctly evaluate the effects of electromagnetic phenomena on the behavior of ICT (and, more generally, electronic) equipments.

Thanks to the approach adopted during the course, at the end the student will have developed the ability to apply standard solutions to the different cases that he may face, and to evaluate their feasibility. He will also be able to build an appropriate model of a physical situation, which then he can solve and interpret the mathematical solutions found.

The knowledge acquired will allow the student to subsequently deal with the study, integration and design of equipment, systems and services that use electromagnetic fields; these will also be useful to those who will not deal directly with these activities, as it will allow future engineers to interact efficiently with the designers of electromagnetic devices, which are increasingly widespread in all electronic and ICT systems, as well as in many systems of diagnostics and measurement, particularly in the physical and biomedical fields.

syllabus_topics: Real transmission lines and matching structures
Dielectric behavior and propagation at RF and microwaves
Theorems of reciprocity, uniqueness and equivalence

assessment_methods.method: Written part (analysis and synthesis problems of small antenna arrays and radio-links)
Oral exam (thorough discussion on one of the course topic)

assessment_rules: The final verification consists of a written part (maximum 14 points) and an oral exam (maximum 20 points). To pass the exam, a student must pass separately the written part (minimum of 5 points) and the oral part (minimum of 12 points), and the sum of the two partial marks must be at least 18. For specific didactic needs related to the epidemiological situation, either the written test or the oral part or both can be held at a distance using computer aids, which may change the maximum and minimum scores. Passing the exam requires a correct knowledge, adequate ability in tool use, and minimum skills, with higher grades reflecting higher ability and skills.
